preview: Ankit Jaiswal shares his Barclays interview experience for the 2022 Summer internship role of Business Analyst - BA3, detailing the online assessment, coding problems, and the combined technical-HR interview.
content:
Interview Experience 
 
Ankit Jaiswal 
TY Computer Engineering
1 
Introduction 
Barclays visited our campus VJTI on 12th Oct 2021, to hire interns for the 2022 Summer internship 
for the role of Business Analyst - BA3. Eligibility criteria were 3rd-year CE and IT students with >= 
60% score across class X and XII and CGPA > 6.75 and no active backlogs. They don’t allow 
Diploma students for the process.  
PPT 
Before the coding round they conducted a PPT on 19th Oct 2021, and this is very important because 
here they discuss about the company and their values (RISES) and purpose. They ask questions 
based on this ppt in HR round so do note the important points. Before the PPT they sent a list of 
shortlisted candidates (57 students).  
Coding Round 
The coding round was also conducted on the same day just after the PPT. The coding round was 
held on Hackerearth platform and it consisted of 30 MCQs and 2 Coding Questions. There was no 
negative marking so here you can attempt all the questions even if you are not sure. You can 
switch between the questions and this was the best part. The MCQs were mostly based on JAVA 
and C++ (almost 50% of the questions were based on this only) and rest were based on MongoDB, 
SQL and Postgre SQL queries, Python, Javascript, Data structures, OS (I didn’t had questions on 
this but some students had OS questions too) and Servlets. Do prepare for the MCQs well because 
it has equal weightage as compared to coding questions. 
Quick Description of all the MCQs: 
• 
Java: Output based questions as well as some other type but I don’t know JAVA much so 
I was unable to understand. 
• 
C++: Output based questions only. Approx. 7-8 questions were based on C++. 
• 
Python: 2 questions and they were too output based 
• 
Javascript: 2 questions and in one question they had given a code and we had to fill in the 
blanks with the options available 
• 
Data Structures: 2-3 questions output based 
• 
Servlets: These questions were tough for me as it was in JAVA and they were basically 
implementation-oriented questions. The questions had a code and we had to tell whether 
the code is right or not and also some were based on theory of servlets.
2 
• 
SQL: Three questions out of which two were basic SQL queries on Union and Joins and 
one was based on some access privileges. 
• 
MongoDB: 2 Questions and they were basically based on connection part of mongo with 
some application. 
Important Tip: The output-based questions can be easily solved with the help the editor provided 
for the coding questions😉. You can simply write the same code in the code editor and try running 
it. I also used this to solve some of the questions😎. 
Coding Questions: 
• 
Maximum Partitions: 
There is an array of N integers, you are given a task to make any number of partitions in the array 
such that the Special Sum of all the partitions combined is maximized. Suppose you make K 
partitions then the Special Sum is defined as P1 - P2 + P3 - P4 + P5 ..... +(-1)(K - 1)Pk. Here Pi is 
defined as summation of all integers in that partition. 
Input: 
• 
The first line of input consists of an integer N, which denotes the number of integers in 
the array.     
• 
The second line of input consist of N integers, which denotes the values of the array. 
Output: 
• 
A single integer which denotes the maximum value of the Special Sum that can be obtained 
by any number of partitions. 
Sample Input: 
5 
1 -2 -3 2 1 
Sample Output: 
9 
• 
Abandoned City: 
You bought a virtual reality glasses. There is only one game installed to it called "The Abandoned 
City". 
You are lost in an abandoned city. In order to escape, you have to pay a number of golden coins. 
So, you decided to collect the gold in the houses of that city. The city contains many houses aligned 
in a straight line. Each house contains a specific amount of golden coins.
3 
You need to figure out the shortest distance you have to walk until you collect the needed amount 
of golden coins to get out. 
Note: You can start from any house i and continue your as i to i+1 or i to i−1 but you can't change 
your direction, and stop at any house.  
Example: 
Let's assume that the number of houses is 5 and coins in those houses are [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] and target 
is 7. It can be seen that to collect 7 coins you will have to travel through at least 2 houses. The 
possible travel options are - 
• 
Start from 3rd house, travel right and stop at 4th or start from 4th house, travel left and stop 
at 3rd house, thus collecting 7 coins. 
• 
Start from 4th house, travel right and stop at 5th or start from 5th house, travel left and stop 
at 4th house, thus collecting 11 coins. 
Thus, the shortest distance you have to walk until you collect 7 golden coins is 2. 
Input: 
• 
The first line contains an integer, n, denoting the number of houses. 
• 
Each line i of the n subsequent lines (where 0≤i<n) contains an integer describing the 
number of coins of the ith house. 
• 
Followed by a line contains an integer, target, denoting the number of the golden coins you 
have to pay to get out of the city. 
Output: 
Print the minimum distance you have to walk to collect the needed amount of golden coins to get 
out or -1 if no such answer exists. 
Code: 
This question can be solved with the help of sliding window but in the worst case it takes O(n2) 
where n is the size of the array. 
#include<iostream> 
#include<bits/stdc++.h> 
using namespace std; 
 
typedef long long ll; 
 
int main(){
4 
    ll n; 
    cin >> n; 
    ll arr[n]; 
 
    for(ll i=0; i < n; i++) 
        cin >> arr[i]; 
     
    ll k; 
    cin >> k; 
     
    ll pre[n + 1]; 
    pre[0] = 0; 
     
    for(ll i=1; i<=n; i++) 
        pre[i] = pre[i-1] + arr[i - 1]; 
     
    if(pre[n] < k) 
        cout << -1 << endl; 
     
    else{ 
        ll ans = INT_MAX; 
        for(ll i=1; i <= n; i++) { 
            ll l = i; 
            ll r = n; 
            ll mid; 
            while(l <= r) { 
                mid = l + (r - l)/2; 
                if(pre[mid] - pre[i-1] >= k){ 
                    ans = min(ans, mid - i + 1); 
                    r = mid - 1; 
                } 
                else 
                    l = mid + 1; 
            } 
        } 
        cout << ans << endl; 
    } 
    return 0; 
}
5 
Interview Round (Technical + HR): 
A total of 18 students were shortlisted for the interview round.  
The interview was conducted at 21st Oct 2021 on WebEx platform. The process started from 5:00 
A.M. Mine slot was at 10:00 A.M. but due to some technical difficulties from the interviewer end the 
interview started on 11:10 A.M. The interview lasted for approx. 40 min. There was only one 
interviewer. 
My interview was almost HR based. My interview started with the basic question Tell me about 
yourself? I was already prepared for this and I introduced myself. As I mentioned my projects in my 
introduction, she began asking me detailed questions about them, such as: 
• 
What is the tech stack used? 
• 
What is the purpose of this project? 
• 
What was the motivation behind making this project? 
Then she started asking me about: 
• 
Quality of team leader according to you? 
• 
Challenges faced while working in a team and how did I mitigate them? 
Make sure that you prepare well for the projects because the interviewer may cross question you 
about the project, the tech stack used and also some were asked to show their code so be honest 
with whatever you put in your resume. 
Then she asked me whether I had used SQL in any of my projects or not? To this I answered yes 
and explained exactly where I used SQL and how did I used it.   
I had mentioned that I am a mentor in Community of Coders Club in my college. She asked me 
about my mentorship and what I exactly did in that. I told her that I am mentoring a few teams under 
one of the programs so a lot of cross questions on that such as: 
• 
What motivates you to do this?  
• 
Qualities of a good mentor according to you? 
• 
Challenges faced? 
Then she asked me questions related to Barclays values (RISES): 
• 
Why Barclays? 
• 
Are you comfortable to work in Pune or Chennai?
6 
Then she asked me whether I had any questions for her. Please do ask questions. This 
demonstrates how interested and enthusiastic you are about this internship. 
I asked her  
• 
Her exact role in Barclays? 
• 
Tech stack that Barclays uses? 
• 
What projects will we be working on during our internship? 
I was very happy with my performance but I was also anxious because I was rejected by many 
companies, despite the fact that my interview had gone well. 
Conclusion: 
The results were announced the following evening, and a total of 13 students were selected for the 
summer internship and I was one of them 😊. 
Important Tips: 
For Coding Round: 
• 
Practice famous problem from 450dsa.com, GeeksForGeeks, and Leetcode.  
• 
Every Company has some type of questions that are asked in every coding round, so do 
check the GFG Internship Archives for that specific company and try to solve all those 
questions. 
• 
Make sure you prepare CS Fundamentals along with DSA. Study them thoroughly, it will 
help you to clear both Online Test as well as Interviews. 
• 
For aptitude questions, practice some problems from Indiabix website. They generally 
include topics like PnC, probability, Work-time related problems, statistics, puzzles, blood 
relation questions etc. 
• 
Generally, you'll get to know the platform for the test one or two days before the test, you 
can try looking for the questions asked in that platform to get an idea of the level of 
questions asked. 
• 
Refer this doc, it will answer most of your questions regarding preparations and resources. 
• 
For OS, DBMS, and OOPs in Java and C++, I prepared from GFG. Be prepared with all the 
concepts from each of them very clearly.
7 
 
 
For Interviews: 
• 
The most important thing is to stay calm and be confident. A lot of weightages are on your 
confidence. 
• 
Join the interview link at least 5 minutes prior the time allotted to you. It gives an impression 
that you are punctual. 
• 
While explaining CS Fundamentals, always try to give a real-world example, if possible, for 
that concept. It gives a positive impression to the interviewer. 
• 
If you don’t know the answer for any specific questions, simply say NO to the interviewer 
rather than bluffing in front of the interviewer. 
• 
Be thorough with your resume. DON’T LIE in your Resume, that’s your true identity, and 
by lying, I mean 
o Skills that you’re not very confident about  
o Position of Responsibilities or Activities you haven’t done  
o Projects in which you barely did anything.  
Basically, Don’t Write Anything You Cannot Take the Conversation Further. 
• 
Be prepared for basic questions like Tell me about yourself. Just try to byheart this 
because in the interview you might tend to forget this. I also did the same thing. 
• 
Try to research about the company and also about the interviewers and do attend the 
PPT because Barclays focus a lot on its PPT. 
• 
Barclays always asks HR questions based on its values (RISES) so do thorough research 
on this. 
• 
Try to connect to the interviewer and make sure that the interviewer is listening to you 
rather than talking alone. 
• 
LUCK🤞 plays a very vital role in the internship drive and try to learn from the rejections. I 
was also rejected by 5 different companies before getting selected. Always try to do learn 
from the mistakes and try to do your best in the next one 😊.  
 
ALL THE BEST 😊👍
